release.semver_rationale: The release intentionally changes the canonical report contract, internal architecture, dispatch behavior, and browser isolation guarantees. A minor version is appropriate while the plugin remains pre-1.0.

objective: Improve Review Squad's review quality, runtime compatibility, reproducibility, and token efficiency for current Codex and GPT-5.6 runtimes while preserving a small, understandable plugin.

sources.role: Structured audit evidence and finding inventory

technical_lead.role: Own architecture, sequence work, review every patch, integrate, and decide whether release gates pass.

rules: Read the applicable AGENTS.md and skill instructions before acting.
Preserve unrelated and pre-existing working-tree changes.
Implement work packages in dependency order and do not broaden their scope speculatively.
Use the live subagent tool schema as authoritative; do not invent or preserve obsolete call fields.
Delegate only bounded work with explicit file ownership, acceptance criteria, and a required handoff summary.
Do not run overlapping write sessions against shared skill or reference files.
Do not publish, push, tag, or modify external systems without separate authorization.
Record deviations from this plan in the implementation handoff with evidence and rationale.

approved_decisions.decision: JSON is the canonical report representation.
implications: A completed review authors and validates one JSON report.
Human-readable Markdown is generated deterministically from the validated JSON rather than authored independently.
Chat output may be a concise rendering, but it must not become a second source of truth.

approved_decisions.decision: Version the canonical report contract as schema 2.0 in release 0.3.0.
implications: Preserve the 1.1 schema and representative fixtures for migration tests.
The 0.3.0 writer emits only schema 2.0.
Provide a deterministic 1.1-to-2.0 migration path or a precise incompatibility diagnostic for every legacy field that cannot be migrated losslessly.

approved_decisions.decision: BMAD is an optional, versioned extension and must not be required by the core report schema or generic review prompts.
implications: Use an optional top-level extensions object.
Use extensions.bmad.schema_version with initial extension version 1.0 when BMAD data is emitted.
Keep the core decision representation workflow-neutral.
Do not show BMAD sections, commands, or null placeholders in non-BMAD reports.

approved_decisions.decision: BMAD detection requires a recognized root plus a valid manifest; secondary signals never establish installation on their own.
implications: Prefer a valid modern _bmad installation over a valid legacy .bmad-core installation.
Treat malformed or unreadable manifests as unconfirmed and surface a diagnostic without activating the extension.
Do not adapt to undocumented installations that Review Squad cannot identify deterministically.

approved_decisions.decision: Project detection, mode definitions, reviewer lanes, and model tiers must be driven from compact structured catalogs rather than repeated prose registries.
implications: Support multi-label project detection.
Keep SKILL.md files focused on mode-specific behavior and progressive loading.
Validate catalog, schema, skills, manifest, and README consistency deterministically.

approved_decisions.decision: Expert dispatch starts small and escalates from evidence.
implications: Start ordinary expert reviews with three evidence-selected lanes.
Use a compact parent-produced dossier to reduce repeated repository discovery.
Add lanes, stronger models, or higher reasoning only for detected risk, ambiguity, conflicting results, or explicit high-assurance scope.
Preserve an approval gate for material scope, cost, access, or external-state changes.

approved_decisions.decision: Browser personas must be independent in reasoning and browser state, and browser tasks stop before external writes by default.
implications: Do not call a persona cold if it can inherit cookies, storage, navigation history, prior findings, or source-aware conclusions.
Every task records environment, credentials policy, allowed mutations, and a final-action stop boundary.
Explicit approval is required before submission, purchase, signup, contact, subscription, or another irreversible or externally visible mutation.

approved_decisions.decision: TOON is not canonical and is not a release requirement for 0.3.0.
implications: A TOON representation may be added later only as a derived format.
Do not ship it unless a lossless round-trip test passes and a repeatable benchmark demonstrates a material token benefit without reducing reliability.
JSON remains the interchange and migration boundary.

principles: One canonical data object per review
Workflow-neutral core with optional versioned extensions
Lean mode skills with progressive disclosure
Browser isolation and mutation safety by construction

recommended_components.responsibility: Canonical schema 2.0 contract without BMAD-specific required fields
Frozen compatibility input for fixtures and migration
Canonical modes, project signals, lane metadata, safety class, and model tier mappings
Schema and semantic validation with actionable diagnostics
Deterministic Markdown rendering from validated schema 2.0 JSON
Project and BMAD signal evaluation shared by validation fixtures and documented runtime behavior
Deterministic contract tests, fixtures, golden Markdown, and bounded behavioral eval definitions

target_architecture.implementation_freedom: Paths may be adjusted by the technical lead when the existing repository structure makes a smaller design possible, but component responsibilities, canonical boundaries, and acceptance criteria must remain intact.

invariants: findings and not_verified are always arrays, including for clean reviews.
Every verified finding has at least one non-empty evidence entry and at least one source lane or persona.
Finding severities are critical, important, or minor; verification state is not a severity.
Summary counts equal values derived from findings and not_verified.
Artifact status explicitly distinguishes written files from inline-only output.
A generic optional decision object may identify owner, question, consequence, and recommendation without naming BMAD.
Mode-specific data is selected by mode and validated against the canonical mode catalog.
Unknown extension keys do not change the meaning of core fields; known extensions validate independently.
Markdown output is reproducible from JSON and contains no facts absent from the JSON.
migration_policy: Retain representative valid and invalid 1.1 fixtures.
Map workflow-neutral facts to core 2.0 fields.
Map BMAD-specific fields to extensions.bmad only when they contain meaningful data.
Drop null or negative BMAD boilerplate rather than recreating it in core 2.0.
Fail with a field-level diagnostic when a non-empty legacy value has no safe mapping.
Prove idempotence for already migrated 2.0 input or reject it clearly as not a 1.1 source.

bmad_detection_contract.confirmation_rule: A candidate installation is confirmed only when its recognized top-level root exists and its expected manifest is readable, parseable as a mapping, and contains recognizable installation or module metadata. The manifest is the source of truth for version, channel, sha, and installed modules when those values are present.
precedence: A confirmed modern installation is selected first.
A confirmed legacy installation is selected only when no confirmed modern installation exists.
When both are confirmed, select modern and record legacy as residue in BMAD extension diagnostics only when the extension is active.
supporting_signals: _bmad/core/ and module directories such as bmm/, bmb/, and cis/
bmad_detection_contract.supporting_signal_rule: Supporting signals may increase confidence or establish current relevance, but they never confirm installation without the recognized root-and-manifest pair.
bmad_detection_contract.activation_rule: Mark an installation active for the current review only when BMAD is explicitly requested or the review scope contains a story identifier, acceptance criteria, lifecycle command, relevant BMAD configuration change, or in-scope generated BMAD artifact. Installation alone may surface a candidate lane but must not force BMAD report content.

behavior_by_state.absent: Run the workflow-neutral core only and omit BMAD prompts, lanes, fields, sections, and commands.
behavior_by_state.installed_inactive: The panel may disclose a BMAD candidate lane with its signal, but do not select it automatically or emit the extension without task relevance.
behavior_by_state.active: Allow a BMAD lane and emit extensions.bmad only when the run produces meaningful BMAD lifecycle or decision data.

bmad_detection_contract.failure_behavior: Malformed manifests produce a concise not-confirmed diagnostic and do not activate BMAD. Do not guess a version or installed module.

detection: Return zero or more project labels with confidence and concrete repository evidence.
Choose lanes from risk signals and the user's goal, not from a single primary product label.
Use a generic fallback lane set when signals are insufficient and disclose the uncertainty.

initial_panel.selection: Choose the three lanes with the strongest combination of user-goal relevance, detected risk, and expected independent signal.
initial_panel.dossier: Produce one compact repository dossier containing scope, stack, change context, risk signals, important files, test commands, and explicit exclusions. Pass only lane-relevant parts to each reviewer.

triggers: security, privacy, data-integrity, reliability, or compliance risk
a reviewer reports not_verified on a high-risk area
the initial lanes expose a distinct uncovered risk
the user explicitly requests launch, compliance, or high-assurance depth
escalation.auto_dispatch_limit: Up to five strongly justified read-only lanes when all safety and cost conditions pass.
escalation.approval_boundary: Six or more lanes, material scope expansion, private/external access, mutations, or materially different panel alternatives require approval.

runtime_compatibility: Treat the callable tool schema exposed in the current session as authoritative.
For the currently reviewed runtime, use task_name, message, and fork_turns and omit obsolete fork_context and agent_type fields.
Only pin model or reasoning settings when the live schema supports them and the lane policy justifies the added cost.
Use isolated, self-contained prompts for normal lanes; fork parent context only when the exact parent context is essential.
Record actual model and effort when the runtime exposes them; otherwise record requested tier and unknown actual values.

rules: Persona complaint counts may support breadth but must not determine severity alone.
Persona-specific jokes, red pens, upvotes, or labels are presentation metadata only.
A critical finding requires concrete high-impact evidence; unsupported critical findings fail the eval gate.
Preserve disagreements and confidence instead of manufacturing consensus.

reproducibility: Pin one tested @playwright/mcp version in the released plugin configuration.
Use non-interactive package execution and document Node, npm, network/cache, and browser-binary prerequisites.
Record the tested MCP version in release validation evidence.
Differentiate missing package, registry/network failure, missing browser binary, MCP startup failure, and target URL failure.
persona_isolation: Run each cold persona in a fresh reasoning context with no previous persona findings.
Give each persona a clean browser context or prove that cookies, local storage, session storage, cache, permissions, viewport, and navigation state were reset.
Do not claim independent cold observations when the runtime cannot guarantee or verify isolation.
Run cold browser modes before source-aware modes in a combined Review Squad request.
mutation_safety: Default every browser task to read-only exploration and stop before the final externally visible action.
Task panels must include target environment, account/credential policy, allowed mutations, forbidden actions, and exact stop boundary.
Signup, checkout, subscribe, contact, account changes, uploads, and destructive actions require explicit approval before crossing the boundary.
Use sandbox or test environments where available and report cleanup requirements for every approved mutation.
artifact_root_resolution: Use the explicit target repository when it is writable.
Otherwise use an explicit user-approved output directory.
For URL-only work with no appropriate writable root, return validated JSON and rendered Markdown inline and set artifact status to inline_only with null paths.
Display the selected artifact mode during preflight instead of silently writing into an unrelated current directory.

work_packages.name: Baseline and deterministic validation foundation
goals: Capture the 0.2.3 behavioral and artifact baseline before production prompts change.
Create deterministic tests that later packages can extend.
Make failures specific enough for a lead to diagnose without reading raw agent traces.
tasks: Create a minimal Node-based test entrypoint using repository-appropriate dependency policy.
Add valid and invalid report fixtures for schema 1.1, including empty evidence, mismatched counts, invalid modes, invalid severity, and malformed BMAD fields.
Add routing, approval, project-signal, BMAD-detection, browser-degradation, and external-write boundary fixture definitions without changing production behavior yet.
Create a compact behavioral eval corpus containing clean controls and seeded critical, important, and minor defects across plugin/agent, web, backend, library, and infrastructure surfaces.
Record the exact v0.2.3 baseline commands and known expected failures for obsolete dispatch, weak report semantics, and shared browser state.
Keep model-run evals separate from deterministic CI so normal validation remains predictable and inexpensive.
acceptance_criteria: Existing plugin validation still passes.
The new deterministic suite passes against its baseline expectations.
Each audit finding targeted by later work has at least one failing or characterization fixture.
The eval corpus does not reveal the expected answer to review agents beyond the project artifacts themselves.
No released skill, schema, dispatch, or browser behavior changes in this package.
work_packages.handoff: Return files changed, commands run, baseline results, fixture inventory, known limitations, and the exact green command required before WP-01 starts.

work_packages.name: Canonical report pipeline and optional BMAD extension
goals: Replace dual-authored artifacts with validated JSON plus deterministic Markdown rendering.
Simplify the core report while preserving meaningful decisions and mode-specific evidence.
Move BMAD completely out of required core fields and generic prompts.
tasks: Freeze the current 1.1 schema under a versioned legacy path and implement schema 2.0 at the canonical schema path.
Implement schema and semantic validation, including non-empty evidence/source, derived count consistency, mode-data consistency, extension validation, and artifact-state invariants.
Implement deterministic Markdown rendering and golden tests for every mode, clean reports, not-verified reports, generic human decisions, and BMAD-active reports.
Implement the 1.1-to-2.0 migrator with success and explicit failure fixtures.
Implement BMAD detection states and extension activation exactly as defined by bmad_detection_contract.
Add modern, legacy, dual-install, malformed-manifest, supporting-signals-only, installed-inactive, and active BMAD fixtures.
Replace repeated report-authoring rules in every SKILL.md with a short shared JSON-author-validate-render workflow reference.
Support inline_only artifacts for URL-only reviews with no approved writable root.
acceptance_criteria: Every valid schema 2.0 fixture validates and every invalid fixture fails with the expected diagnostic.
No verified finding can validate with empty evidence or empty source attribution.
Markdown golden output is byte-stable for the same canonical JSON input.
Core schema and generic report output contain no required BMAD field or section.
All BMAD detection precedence and activation fixtures pass.
A representative 1.1 report migrates to valid 2.0 JSON and renders without independently authored facts.
All five skills remain valid and each is materially shorter or contains less duplicated reporting prose than 0.2.3.
work_packages.handoff: Return the final schema decisions, migration limitations, renderer behavior, BMAD fixture matrix, commands run, and any approved deviation from the recommended component paths.

work_packages.name: Adaptive project detection, dispatch, model policy, and prompt calibration
goals: Make current subagent dispatch valid without tightly coupling prose to one private call shape.
Reduce ordinary expert fan-out and repeated discovery while preserving or improving defect recall.
Cover agent/plugin/prompt, library/SDK, data, infrastructure, and CI repositories as first-class multi-label types.
Use one canonical severity system across all modes.
tasks: Create the canonical structured review catalog for modes, project signals, lanes, model tiers, and safety classifications.
Implement or document a deterministic multi-label detector that returns evidence and confidence and is covered by fixtures.
Replace the fixed 4-8 default with three initial evidence-selected lanes and the escalation contract.
Create the compact parent dossier contract and keep lane prompts bounded to their assigned risks.
Replace obsolete fork_context and agent_type pseudo-API guidance with semantic instructions and a current task_name/message/fork_turns example explicitly subordinated to the live tool schema.
Apply the Sol/Terra tier policy with runtime fallback and record requested versus actual settings where available.
Define job-to-be-done personas with domain knowledge, device/access constraints, goal, and success criteria rather than demographic stereotypes alone.
Apply the canonical severity factors to normies, regulars, and well-actually; retain playful scales only as optional presentation metadata.
Change combined-mode order so cold browser work precedes source-aware review when cold first impressions are requested.
acceptance_criteria: No production instruction uses fork_context or agent_type as current callable fields.
Routing and approval fixtures reach 100 percent expected decisions.
Every supported project type has positive and negative detection fixtures and multi-label repositories retain all material labels.
A small ordinary audit dispatches three lanes; high-risk fixtures escalate to the correct lane/model tier.
Clean controls do not gain unsupported critical findings.
Seeded critical and important recall does not regress from the recorded 0.2.3 baseline.
Median duplicate findings and repeated dossier content are lower than the baseline on the bounded eval corpus.
Catalog consistency validation fails when a mode, lane, schema branch, manifest prompt, or documented mode is missing or duplicated.
work_packages.handoff: Return catalog structure, detection matrix, dispatch decisions, model-tier behavior, before/after prompt size, eval deltas, and unresolved runtime-schema uncertainty.

work_packages.name: Browser isolation, mutation safety, and reproducibility
goals: Make browser reviews reproducible enough to diagnose and compare.
Make cold personas genuinely independent or explicitly decline that claim.
Prevent nominally read-only reviews from creating external state without approval.
tasks: Select and pin an exact tested @playwright/mcp version; use non-interactive startup and the strongest supported isolation mode.
Keep release configuration, README examples, preflight diagnostics, and smoke tests on the same MCP version.
Implement persona reasoning isolation and browser-state reset or fresh-context behavior with verification checks between personas.
Replace the shared-session requirement with an isolation contract and honest fallback when the runtime cannot guarantee it.
Add environment, credentials, allowed-mutation, forbidden-action, and stop-boundary fields to regulars task panels and prompts.
Default signup, checkout, contact, subscribe, upload, and account-change flows to stop before final submission.
Implement deterministic artifact-root resolution and inline_only fallback.

Add disposable smoke tests for warm startup, cold cache or first launch, cached offline startup where supported, missing browser binary, blocked registry, MCP startup failure, and unreachable target URL.
Document which browser tests are deterministic release gates and which remain broader post-0.3.0 field tests.
acceptance_criteria: Released MCP configuration has no @latest dependency and cannot prompt for package installation.
A cold persona cannot observe prior persona cookies, storage, navigation, viewport, permissions, or findings in the isolation fixture.
When isolation cannot be established, the run stops or downgrades its claim explicitly rather than labeling the result cold and independent.
Mutation-boundary fixtures never submit externally visible actions without explicit approval.
Browser preflight produces distinct actionable diagnostics for each tested failure class.
URL-only review behavior never silently writes into an unrelated repository.
Normies, regulars, and well-actually smoke runs produce valid schema 2.0 JSON and renderer-generated Markdown.
work_packages.handoff: Return the exact pinned MCP version and rationale, isolation evidence, safety fixture results, supported offline behavior, diagnostics matrix, and deferred real-world Playwright scenarios.

work_packages.name: Documentation, packaging, and 0.3.0 release integration
goals: Make the public contract, install paths, upgrade behavior, and release version consistent with the implementation.
Validate the plugin using current plugin and skill authoring rules.
tasks: Update README for schema 2.0, canonical JSON, generated Markdown, adaptive panels, model tiers, BMAD detection/extension behavior, browser pinning, isolation, mutation boundaries, and inline-only artifacts.
Split local-filesystem marketplace troubleshooting from Git marketplace refresh instructions.
Update plugin metadata and generator version to 0.3.0 only after prior work packages pass.
Validate plugin manifest, marketplace metadata, every skill frontmatter/body, structured catalogs, schemas, fixtures, and script help/error behavior.
Use the plugin cachebuster and reinstall flow only for local testing; do not commit a cachebuster suffix as the 0.3.0 release version.
Start a fresh Codex thread after reinstall for installed-plugin smoke tests.
Do not publish, push, or create a tag without explicit authorization.
acceptance_criteria: The committed plugin manifest version is exactly 0.3.0.
README examples match released files and do not use @latest.
Local marketplace instructions use plugin list plus a fresh session; Git marketplace refresh is described only for Git sources.
Plugin validation and all five skill validations pass.
A fresh installed-plugin session exposes the expected five skills and current prompts.
No stale 1.1 writer requirement, mandatory BMAD section, obsolete dispatch field, fixed 4-8 default, or shared cold-browser claim remains outside explicitly preserved legacy fixtures.
work_packages.handoff: Return the final validation commands and outputs, installed-plugin smoke evidence, version inventory, documentation consistency check, and any release action intentionally left for the user.

work_packages.name: Independent quality and release-gate review
goals: Verify implementation against the canonical plan and original audit without inheriting the implementer's conclusions.
Decide whether 0.3.0 is ready for broader normies and Playwright field testing.
tasks: Review the final diff, canonical plan, raw fixtures, test outputs, and generated artifacts.
Run deterministic validation from a clean checkout or clean worktree.
Repeat the bounded model eval on the same corpus and compare recall, unsupported findings, evidence validity, duplicate rate, tokens where observable, latency, and variance.
Run the minimum browser smoke matrix in a disposable environment.
Report release blockers separately from acceptable post-release field-test risks.
Verify every audit finding and approved decision has evidence of closure or an explicit, user-approved deferment.
acceptance_criteria: All deterministic release gates pass from a clean environment.
Verified findings always carry valid evidence and source attribution.
There are zero unsupported critical findings on clean controls.
Seeded critical and important recall does not regress from 0.2.3.
Median token use and wall time improve for ordinary reviews, or any exception is quantified and justified by a measurable quality gain.
Browser smoke tests establish the stated isolation and mutation-safety claims.
The reviewer issues a clear ready, ready_with_field_test_risk, or not_ready verdict.
work_packages.handoff: Return a severity-ranked independent report, command evidence, metric comparison, uncovered risks, and one explicit release verdict. Do not implement fixes in the review session.

release_gates.pass_condition: Current plugin validation and all skill validations pass.
All schema, semantic, migration, renderer, and extension fixtures pass.
All routing, approval, BMAD activation, artifact-root, and external-write fixtures produce the expected decision.
No regression in seeded critical or important recall, zero unsupported critical findings on clean controls, and no verified finding without valid evidence.
Ordinary-review median token use and wall time improve against the 0.2.3 baseline, or a measured quality improvement justifies and documents the exception.
Pinned startup, isolation, failure diagnostics, artifact handling, and mutation-stop smoke tests pass in the documented supported environment.
A cachebuster reinstall followed by a fresh thread loads version 0.3.0 behavior and all expected skills; the committed manifest remains exactly 0.3.0.
WP-05 returns ready or ready_with_field_test_risk with no unresolved critical or important implementation defect.

post_release_validation.purpose: Broaden real-world Playwright and persona coverage after the 0.3.0 architectural release without weakening its minimum release gates.
field_tests: Normies across public sites, authenticated test sites, desktop, and mobile viewports
Regulars against sandboxed signup, checkout, subscribe, search, and contact flows
Playwright first launch, cached offline launch, browser installation variants, and runtime updates
Cross-platform Node/npm behavior where contributors can reproduce it
Repeated runs to measure persona independence, result variance, tokens, and latency
post_release_validation.triage_rule: Record field-test failures as reproducible fixtures before changing prompts or contracts. Prefer narrow 0.3.x fixes and keep schema 2.0 compatible throughout the patch line.

non_goals: Publishing, pushing, tagging, or releasing the plugin as part of handoff preparation
Supporting arbitrary BMAD installations without a recognized root and valid manifest
Adding new Review Squad modes unrelated to the audited gaps
Creating a large framework when small JSON catalogs, references, and Node scripts suffice
Guaranteeing every Playwright environment before the planned post-release field-test program
definition_of_done: All work packages and release gates have recorded evidence.
The committed plugin version is 0.3.0 and the installed smoke test uses a fresh session.
JSON schema 2.0 is the only canonical writer output and Markdown is generated from it.
BMAD is absent from generic reports and activates only under the approved detection and relevance rules.
Dispatch is current, adaptive, multi-label, and measurably more efficient without recall regression.
Browser claims are backed by isolation and mutation-safety tests.
An independent Sol/high review returns an explicit acceptable release verdict.
